title: From Clinical Judgment to Checkable Rules: Clinician-Led Guardrails for Mental-Health Chatbots
abstract: arXiv:2610.30690v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) deployed in mental-health contexts can be evaluated for safety failures, but the resulting judgments are often difficult to inspect or explain. Common approaches to improving safety rely on prompt engineering, LLM-as-a-Judge, and Constitutional AI. In this work, we describe a clinician-led alternative in which two clinicians define, finalize, and adjudicate the four safety checks of a rule base, which is formally verified for internal consistency and applied as a guardrail over LLM outputs. Here and in the title, clinician-led refers to this rule base, not to the fact extractor or the uncertainty default, which are ours. Every verdict of the resulting verification layer is recomputable from a named rule and sixteen facts. Against an LLM judge matched in model, revision, quantization, rule text, and decoding but without the layer's computed 988/911 fact, the largest disagreement class, the satisfied-rule class

translated_title: 从临床判断到可核查规则：由临床医生主导的心理健康聊天机器人安全护栏
translated_abstract: 在心理健康场景中部署的大语言模型（LLM）虽然可以对安全性失效进行评估，但由此产生的判断往往难以审查或解释。提升安全性的常见方法依赖于提示工程、LLM-as-a-Judge（以大模型作为评判者）以及宪法AI（Constitutional AI）。在本工作中，我们提出了一种由临床医生主导的替代方案：由两名临床医生定义、确定并裁决规则库中的四项安全检查，该规则库经过形式化验证以确保内部一致性，并作为护栏应用于大语言模型的输出之上。在本文及标题中，“临床医生主导”指的是这一规则库本身，而非事实提取器或不确定性默认处理机制——这两者是我们的贡献。由此产生的验证层所做的每一个判定，都可以通过一条具名规则和十六项事实重新计算得出。与一个在模型、版本、量化、规则文本和解码设置上均完全一致、但缺少该层所计算的988/911求助热线事实的LLM评判者相比，最大的分歧类别——即规则被满足的类别——
tldr: 该论文提出由临床医生主导定义并经形式化验证的安全规则库，将专家临床判断转化为可解释、可复查、可重算的心理健康聊天机器人安全护栏。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a clinician-led, formally verified rule base that transforms expert clinical safety judgments into explainable, auditable, and recomputable guardrails for mental-health chatbots.
